correctness.rationale: For fixed length, the 2-binomial signature is exactly the binary one-count and positional one-moment. Alignments of the 2-uniform complementary morphism prove that an odd root must start at odd index and force source 0^(h+1)1^(h+1) or its complement; avoidance of triple equal symbols forbids all odd roots >=5. Literal witnesses cover roots 1 and 3. All even roots have explicit substitution-based constructions using the exact binary digit-sum complement identity. Primitive substitution factor frequencies and solved pair/triple recurrence equations give density 1/12. Independent exact subsequence counts agree with all tested samples; finite evidence is distinguished from proofs.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2013 and 2015 primary articles concern definitions, avoidance, and binomial factor-class complexity; 2017 treats coarser abelian squares, and 2018/2020 treats k-binomial factor-class complexity. None of these source statements determines occurrence of adjoining 2-binomial-equivalent blocks by half-length or their odd-root density. Record and historical comparisons revealed no equivalent or stronger direct claim. An earlier unindexed derivation remains possible.
residual_risks: Historical mathematical search, research-record indexing and inspected primary texts do not rule out unindexed prior derivations.
The 2018 master thesis cited by Lejeune–Leroy–Rigo was not inspected in full; it concerns factor-class complexity and has not been shown to contain this adjacency spectrum.

value.rationale: The half-length spectrum for 2-binomial squares is a natural refinement of the established morphic repetition-avoidance and abelian-square-abundance problems. It is an exact infinite classification, sharply separates all even lengths from all odd lengths >=5, provides explicit witnesses and an exact positive density for the exceptional odd root. It is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a known-table recomputation; it reveals the effect of a strictly intermediate repetition equivalence.
